observations.seen: No seabed, reef, terrain, or water volume; just floating translucent discs and cylinders in a black void.
Cylinders, boxes, tori, and kitbashed cube clusters; no authored silhouettes.
Effectively untextured; flat tint plus one dithered ring texture.
Everything is either flat translucent teal or additive emissive; no material differentiation.
No roughness or metal response anywhere; nothing reads as steel, rock, or coral.
Emissives are the only light read; no key light direction, no headlight, no falloff on surfaces.
None visible, so nothing grounds the objects.
Uniform flat teal ambient with no occlusion or depth gradient.
No environment reflections or specular at all.
Emissive caps clip to pure white and the rest crushes to black; no highlight rolloff.
Palette is coherent (cyan/teal plus orange accent) but monochrome and blacks are crushed.
Edges look acceptable at desktop res; translucent overlaps hide the worst of it (partly inferred).
Bloom only, overdriven into haze blobs; no fog, DOF, grading, or underwater distortion.
Ring and streak effects exist but are generic, overbright, and semantically unclear.
Comet streaks are large, uniform, and read as projectiles rather than marine snow or bubbles.
No pose or motion cues; static props, no thrust wake or prop wash.
The player sub is either cropped offscreen or indistinguishable from wreck clutter.
Steep top-down, the hero is not framed, and the near-plane foreground clutter is cropped.
No focal point; the centre is empty and bright blobs sit at the frame edges.
No ground, fog falloff, or known-size references, so distance is unreadable.
No underwater fog colour, god rays, caustics, or suspended particulate; the void is black.
The HUD carries the game; in-world you can't tell sub vs wreck vs pickup vs hazard.
Clean, consistent sci-fi panels with good hierarchy, but too many panels and keyboard legends left on screen.
Legible mono/sans pairing with sensible color coding; small sizes on desktop.
No feedback moments visible; the bloom does all the work.
UI eats over half the screen, a panel overlaps the reticle, and the world is a cropped sliver.
Programmer-art prototype with a decent HUD skin.
